$comment: Generation-parameter contract v1. Every payload case must be driven through a production request builder; tests must not synthesize request JSON. Missing overrides are omitted, while numeric zero is an explicit value. Unknown enum values are preserved by contract decoders and must not crash a whole profile. The fixture groups that exercise these rules (cases, resolverCases, wireHardeningCases, relayWireRoundTrips, availabilityCases, lifecycleCases, outboundCases, additionalBodyCases, localEngineCases, llamacppMigrationCases) live next to this file in generation_parameter_contract.v1.cases.json; this file carries rules and tables only.

presentationClasses.$comment: Engineering support states collapse into 3 user-visible classes plus one silent class. All clients read this table only — no client keeps a separate support-label switch of its own. `en` records the English copy each key resolves to, so the table is readable without opening the localization files; labelKey and detailKey are the stable per-client localization keys and remain the only thing a client reads. Adding a new engineering state must register it in both schema.support and supportMap in the same change; the presentation suites on all three clients (web/apps/app/lib/core/chat/__tests__/generation-support-presentation.contract.test.ts, ios/Oriveo/OriveoTests/GenerationParameterSupportPresentationTests.swift, android/app/src/test/java/ai/oriveo/community/core/provider/GenerationParameterSupportPresentationContractTest.kt) walk this table entry by entry and fail on an unmapped state — silently falling back to "no data" is not allowed.

classes.rationale: Silent by default: printing an "already supported" line under every parameter would drown out the states that actually need attention.
Unverified does not mean unsupported: the value still goes out on the wire as-is; the label only states honestly that it has not been verified.

primaryAction.en: See models that support this parameter

classes.rationale: Graying a control out must come with an actionable next step, otherwise it is a dead end for the user.
"We don't know" is shown as exactly that, not rendered as a false conclusion.

accepted_unverified.en: This value is sent to the provider as-is, but we have not verified that it takes effect.

fixed.en: Fixed by the model; changing it has no effect.

unsupported.en: This model does not accept this parameter; sending it will be rejected.

mode_dependent.en: Depends on the current thinking tier; it may change when you switch tiers.

unknown.en: We do not have official information about this parameter yet.

future_supported.en: Announced by the provider, but not available yet.

wireHardening.$comment: The wire path declared in the catalog is the write path; clients trust its semantics, not its shape: thresholds, enums and tiers are entirely catalog-authoritative, but a structurally invalid write path must be rejected by the same rule on every client. A violating parameter is dropped and logged as a local diagnostic; it must never throw and abort the whole request.

availabilityRules.$comment: Defines the three visibility predicates shared by every client. Generation parameters are judged by their declared support state together with the exact profile / transport facts; providerKind plays no part in support semantics. accepted / accepted_unverified / unknown all mean there is no official evidence against the parameter: it is only editable and attempted on the wire when the user has set an explicit value, the wire path is valid, and the current profile identity is complete; future_supported is an explicit official statement that the capability is not yet available, and counts as evidence against adjusting it. Any difference for a relay only comes from the connection identity discovered locally, the final transport, and the profile facts. Each case's profile contains only the one parameter it is about, so entryVisible is always equal to inScope.
sessionActionable: group !== "reasoning" and id does not start with "reasoning_"
support ∈ {supported, accepted, accepted_unverified, unknown}, and the current exact connection × model × final transport/profile identity is complete
independent of any access gating: filtering for the engine_runtime group is applied by each client's own panel on top of this
connectionConfigurable: Does not filter out any row by support: this set is a **rendering surface**, not an interactive one. The unsupported / fixed / mode_dependent / future_supported states are always rendered and grayed out, with the presentationClasses not_adjustable class supplying the reason and the primary action; dropping the row entirely would make the "not adjustable" class structurally unreachable, which is exactly the shape this rule prevents
group !== "engine_runtime", unless the connection is explicitly allowed to manage its own runtime settings
keeps the reasoning group (the connection-level reasoning value is sent on the wire by default)
does not require the wire path to be non-empty: when there is no wire path, the row is still rendered but with editable=false
editable: support ∈ {supported, accepted, accepted_unverified, unknown}, and the current exact profile identity is complete; accepted / accepted_unverified / unknown still require an explicit value before they are actually sent on the wire
availabilityRules.tg6: editable is a subset of the states that can produce a legitimate outbound intent: every providerKind is judged only by support and the exact profile / transport identity; accepted / accepted_unverified / unknown are writable only once identity is complete, and still require an explicit value before being sent. Client-side consumer tests must assert each case individually and must not assert inScope alone.

lifecycleRules.$comment: Defines the lifecycle of a parameter value. dormant is a **derived state**: it equals the current device's judgment of a stored value under the current profile; it is never written to local storage or into the generation_parameter_sync.v1 envelope — each client computes it for itself. Every client consumes this table and must not duplicate the rule elsewhere. ⚠️ This table and capability_evidence_contract.v1.json's official.explicit.* are two projections of the same policy: that one decides requestPolicy (allow_explicit_unverified vs omit_*), this one decides lifecycle (active vs dormant). The two must stay in lockstep — "explicit intent + no official counter-evidence → allow" and "officially-evidenced unsupported / conflict / already rejected upstream → do not allow". Changing the rule on only one side reopens the exact gap this table exists to close.
lifecycleRules.definition: active means the parameter id still goes out on the wire under the current profile; dormant means the value stays in storage and sync but is not currently sent. The two are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
lifecycle: the profile does not declare this parameter id → dormant
the wire path is missing or empty → dormant

the user has expressed explicit intent for this parameter (storedState ∈ {value, omit}; inherit does not count) and there is no official evidence against it — support ∈ {unknown, accepted, accepted_unverified} — → active (unverified does not mean unsupported. **providerKind plays no part in this decision**; a relay's unknown state is just one instance of this same rule. The UI labels it through presentationClasses, whose labelKey and detailKey resolve to the localized copy.)
everything else (unsupported / fixed / mode_dependent / future_supported — these four states are all **conclusions backed by official evidence**, not a metadata gap) → dormant

once the upstream runtime has deterministically rejected this parameter (a negative-cache hit, or the facade judging it omit_runtime_rejected) → dormant; the panel shows "already rejected upstream" with a one-tap resend action
lifecycleRules.valueIndependence: The decision **only looks at whether the parameter id can go out under the current profile, never at the value itself**. An out-of-range value or an enum value outside the known set is a compatibility hint for the user to fix themselves; judging it dormant instead would be just another form of the silent substitution this contract forbids.
lifecycleRules.outboundParity: This table and applyGenerationParameters's outbound gate must stay in lockstep case by case: the set judged active on the read side must equal the set actually written into the body on the send side. Any drift between the two produces a summary that says N items were kept while M items actually went out.
storage: A dormant value is **never deleted**: it stays in the local record and automatically becomes active again once the profile matches, with no need for the user to re-enter it.

A scope record's identity equals connection × model × session, **and never includes the profile fingerprint**. Folding the fingerprint into that identity would cause whole-record invalidation and orphaned records that can no longer be read back.
The fingerprint is a property of the record: it is updated with the current scope on write, and on read it is handed to this table to be judged field by field.
sync: The envelope adds no new dormant field, and schemaVersion stays at 1; an older client reads exactly the same payload shape.

Reason: dormancy is derived locally on each device. Writing it onto the wire would let device A's profile turn off a value on device B that B could actually still send — a cross-device silent substitution.
A dormant value still takes part in export/merge/tombstoning as normal; deletion follows the existing tombstone rule, and an old record is never revived.
ui: When a dormant value exists, a summary row appears at the bottom of the container with two secondary actions, "view" and "clear"; when none exists, the row is not rendered at all.

Both the empty and non-empty states **must be rendered**: after the runtime corrects the transport, the panel is usually non-empty and only missing a subset of parameters; rendering only the empty state would leave dormant values in the non-empty state as silent orphans.
"Clear" only removes the dormant half; the active values are left untouched.
Once the profile matches again, a one-time toast reports how many values were restored.
Copy is resolved from the generationParameterDormant* localization keys; implementation words like dormant, sleeping or frozen must never appear in it.
presets: A preset's identity equals connection × model, matching the scope record's identity, and **never includes the profile fingerprint**. Folding the fingerprint into the match would mean a whole preset becomes unreadable after switching endpoint or protocol, even while the underlying record stays on disk and keeps syncing.
Copying a preset across models is only ever allowed through a field-by-field portable mapping declared for the same provider and the target profile; any field without a mapping is never copied.

Neither saving nor applying a preset **filters values by the current device's active/dormant judgment**: dormancy is a locally derived state, and using it to trim a preset that gets synced elsewhere would let device A's profile turn off a value on device B that B could still send; also, when the profile can't be evaluated at all, every value is judged dormant, so filtering by active would save the preset as empty.

Once applied, the values that land in a scope record are judged field by field by this same table as usual: the ones that don't take effect stay in storage and count toward the dormant-value summary the panel shows, with the outbound gate guaranteeing they are not sent.

outboundRules.$comment: Per-item evaluation in the outbound writer. An invalid item drops only itself and everything else is still sent; the writer returns the list of dropped items (parameterId + reason) so the interface can mark them, instead of expressing the problem as a failure of the whole group. Every client's applyGenerationParameters implementation must pass each entry in outboundCases.
outboundRules.invalidValue: state=value with no value, a type that does not match valueSchema, a value outside range, or one not in enumValues → reason=invalid_value, and only that item is dropped; numbers are never silently clamped or rounded (that would be a silent substitution)

conflict.rule: Items are admitted one by one in the order profile.parameters declares them; a later item that declares conflictsWith against an already admitted item or a presence key the builder already wrote (either direction counts) is dropped with reason=conflict
conflict.invalidItemsDoNotConflict: An item already dropped for invalid_value takes no part in conflict evaluation and must not push any other item out

outboundRules.requires: An item whose requires is not satisfied drops only itself, reason=requirement_unmet
outboundRules.requiredField: state=omit on one of this template's requiredWireFields does not remove the field: the default the builder wrote stays as is, reason=required_field; state=value is unaffected

notes: While thinking is on, a user-set temperature or top_k is not sent, and a top_p below topPMin is not sent, reason=thinking_incompatible

A user-set max tokens that is not greater than the thinking budget is not sent (reason=thinking_budget) and max_tokens goes back to the builder default; if the default is still not greater than the budget, it becomes budget + maxTokensFloorHeadroom
Thinking is written by the capability writer after the generation parameters, so this rule must be evaluated once that writer has finished; with thinking off this rule changes no field

valueSources.$comment: The resolved result carries its source so the conversation screen can show the value actually in effect. layer is the overridePriority layer name; presentation is one of the three source words the interface uses. An explicit omit carries its source layer too.

additionalBodyRules.$comment: Additional request body. A user-supplied JSON object merged into the outgoing request, alongside the generation parameters the catalog declares; the declared custom fields of the web-search and thinking owners are unchanged. This table fixes the rules ahead of the client implementations.
additionalBodyRules.appliesTo: Every BYOK and custom LLM connection
additionalBodyRules.rejection: Rejected on device: no request is sent and the connection is not marked as failing; protected_field and blocked_segment must name the offending field (the interface then points at the line)

merge.panelParameters: Coexist: writing an additional request body does not clear the panel parameters

additionalBodyRules.storage: local_only: never part of the sync envelope, a backup export, telemetry or a diagnostics report
additionalBodyRules.recovery: "Retry without the additional request body" is offered only for an upstream 400 where the final request body really carried the additional body, no upstream event had arrived yet and no tool side effect happened; the action affects that one request and leaves the stored content untouched

localEngineRules.$comment: Transports and parameter tables for engines that run a model on the user's own hardware. The sources are each engine's official documentation and source code; the llama.cpp defaults were additionally checked against /props on a real local llama-server. The parameter tables are constants built into each client (wireHardening.relaySynthesizedWireSource) and every client reconciles them row by row with localEngineProfiles; support is always accepted_unverified and source is always user_declared.
localEngineRules.llamacppChatByDefault: A llama.cpp connection uses /v1/chat/completions by default, so llama-server applies the chat template that ships with the model; the native /completion endpoint flattens the conversation into plain text and bypasses the template, so it is only available as a manual choice

llamacppMigration.rule: An existing connection with engineProfile=llamacpp and transport=llamacpp_native switches once to openai_chat_completions after upgrading, and resolvedAPIBaseURL gains /v1; this runs once per device, and a native transport the user picks afterwards is never rewritten again
llamacppMigration.storedValues: Stored parameter values are not deleted: parameters both transports declare keep working (the wire for max tokens changes from n_predict to max_tokens), and the ones only the native transport declares (n_probs) are treated as "kept, currently not in effect"

localEngineRules.numericTypes: A parameter whose valueSchema is number / integer must go out as a JSON number; llama-server answers a numeric field sent as a string with a 400 (type must be number, but is string) rather than ignoring it silently
localEngineRules.vllmTopLevel: vLLM's extended sampling parameters (top_k, min_p, repetition_penalty, min_tokens, ignore_eos, skip_special_tokens) sit flat at the top level of the request body; extra_body is only an argument name of the OpenAI Python client, and that layer does not exist when sending HTTP directly
localEngineRules.parameterGroups: The sampling, repetition-penalty, budget and output-contract groups are available on every connection; these tables do not use the engine_runtime group
localEngineRules.ollamaOpenAICompat: Ollama goes through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and its table holds only the fields that endpoint's documentation lists; num_ctx and keep_alive are runtime resource settings and are not part of this table

notInTables.$comment: runtime_items are runtime resource settings and stay out of the ordinary generation settings; the value shapes under additional_body_only have no matching panel control and are sent through the additional request body
